messages.content: From my perspective as an experienced cyclist, I prefer Design Scenario 3. The lane width is adequate for my needs. While I don't need the buffer, it does keep cars from drifting into my space. This design supports efficient riding at speed.

As a regular cyclist, I prefer Design Scenario 3 because it strikes the right balance for me. The clear lane markings help define my space. The buffer zone reduces my stress level significantly. This design would make this a regular route for me.

From my nervous cyclist perspective, I strongly prefer Design Scenario 2. Though I still have serious safety concerns without physical protection. Without clear visual separation, I remain very anxious. I need maximum protection to feel safe.

If forced to choose, Design Scenario 2 is the least terrifying option, but I still wouldn't cycle. Without physical protection, this confirms why I don't cycle. Nothing here would convince me to start cycling.

From a driver's perspective, these bike lane options present trade-offs. The protected designs offer better safety for cyclists, but they take up more road space that we need for turning lanes and parking. I hope we can find a balance that works for everyone.
